title: Chemical Engineering and Artificial Intelligence, BSChE (Boston)
overview: The Boston BSChE combines chemical engineering with artificial intelligence methods for predictive models, process optimization and experimental design. The published degree requires 134 semester hours. The award is BSChE, retained as other in the normalized award enum.

courses.name: Cornerstone of Engineering 1
courses.description: Introduces engineering design and programming through projects, laboratories and an original design solution.

category_review.locator: GE 1501 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Hands-on engineering design and prototypes are the organizing domain practice; programming and graphics are supporting tools.

courses.name: Cornerstone of Engineering 2
courses.description: Continues project-based engineering design with analysis, programming, ethical reasoning and working prototypes.
courses.prerequisites: GE 1501 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or ENGR 150M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: GE 1502 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The course continues engineering analysis, design, modeling and prototype construction using software and ethical reasoning as tools.

courses.name: Discrete Structures
courses.description: Develops discrete structures, logic, proofs and counting methods for computing.

category_review.locator: CS 1800 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Sets, relations, induction, proof, logic and counting form discrete mathematical methods; computing motivates their use.

courses.name: Introduction to Program Design and Implementation
courses.description: Introduces programming, dataset analysis and ethical issues in software design.

category_review.locator: CS 2000 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The course teaches program construction, coding and introductory data processing to students without programming experience.

courses.name: Lab for CS 2000
courses.description: Provides experiments supporting introductory programming coursework.

category_review.locator: CS 2001 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The lab explicitly accompanies the introductory program-design course and practices its computing topics.

courses.name: Program Design and Implementation 1
courses.description: Develops program design, object-oriented abstractions and software engineering practices.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 200M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: CS 2100 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Data/object-oriented design, data structures, abstraction, testing and software construction are the central methods.

courses.name: Lab for CS 2100
courses.description: Provides experiments supporting program design coursework.

category_review.locator: CS 2101 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The lab explicitly accompanies the reviewed program-design and software-construction course.

courses.name: Introduction to Databases
courses.description: Develops relational database design, SQL and introductory database-system techniques.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 200M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2500 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D- or EECE 2560 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: CS 3200 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Relational database design, query processing, indexing, concurrency and recovery are database-system methods.

courses.name: Advanced Programming with Data
courses.description: Develops robust software architectures and data pipelines using substantial datasets.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 3500 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Software architectures, reusable APIs, testing and maintainable data pipelines center on general software design and implementation.

courses.name: Mathematical Foundations of Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Studies the mathematical basis of AI through linear algebra, probability and computational exercises.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2510 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 3000 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The description explicitly emphasizes linear algebra, probability and numerical mathematical foundations, using AI as their motivating application.

courses.name: Information Presentation and Visualization
courses.description: Studies how to design, implement and evaluate visual representations of data.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2510 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 4200 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Visualization combines programming, perception, visual communication and domain presentation; the description does not establish one defensible primary category among these.

courses.name: Large-Scale Information Storage and Retrieval
courses.description: Studies scalable data storage, distributed databases and retrieval methods.
courses.prerequisites: ( CS 3100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 310M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 3500 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 3500 with a minimum grade of D- ); CS 3200 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 4300 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Distributed databases, storage architectures, reliability and data retrieval are computing infrastructure methods.

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.description: Introduces predictive modeling and major supervised and unsupervised learning methods.
courses.prerequisites: DS 3000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 250M with a minimum grade of D- or ( MATH 2331 with a minimum grade of D- ; MATH 3081 with a minimum grade of D- )

category_review.locator: DS 4400 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Supervised and unsupervised learning, predictive models, model evaluation and learning algorithms are the explicit central content.

courses.name: Calculus 1 for Science and Engineering
courses.description: Develops differentiation, its scientific applications, and introductory integration.

category_review.locator: MATH 1341 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Limits, differentiation, integration and the fundamental theorem of calculus are the central content.

courses.name: Calculus 2 for Science and Engineering
courses.description: Continues integration methods, series, and introductory vectors and spatial motion.
courses.prerequisites: Additional course-description condition: MATH 1341 or permission of head mathematics advisor.

category_review.locator: MATH 1342 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Integration techniques, infinite series and vectors are the central mathematical topics.

courses.name: Calculus 3 for Science and Engineering
courses.description: Develops multivariable differentiation, multiple integrals and vector calculus.

category_review.locator: MATH 2321 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Multivariable calculus, vector fields and integration theorems are the taught mathematical methods.

courses.name: Differential Equations and Linear Algebra for Engineering
courses.description: Combines differential-equation methods and linear algebra for engineering applications.

category_review.locator: MATH 2341 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Differential equations, numerical methods, transforms and linear algebra are the taught methods, with engineering applications.

courses.name: Probability and Statistics
courses.description: Develops probability distributions and limit theory, then introduces statistical inference.
courses.prerequisites: MATH 1342 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 211M with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1252 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1242 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: MATH 3081 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Probability distributions, expectation, limit theorems and statistical inference are the core content.

category_review.locator: MATH 3082 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The recitation explicitly reinforces the reviewed probability/statistics course.

courses.name: Physics for Engineering 1
courses.description: Develops calculus-based mechanics and fluid physics for engineering.
courses.prerequisites: MATH 1241 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1251 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1340 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1341 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 21EM with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1342 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 211M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 2321 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 316M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: PHYS 1151 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course studies Newtonian mechanics, motion, forces, energy and fluids in engineering physics; calculus is a tool for physical problems, not the principal subject.

courses.name: Lab for PHYS 1151
courses.description: Investigates introductory engineering physics through laboratory experiments.

category_review.locator: PHYS 1152 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Experiments accompany PHYS 1151 engineering mechanics and fluids; the laboratory subject is physical science.

courses.name: Interactive Learning Seminar for PHYS 1151
courses.description: Practices mathematical problem solving in mechanics and fluids.

category_review.locator: PHYS 1153 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The seminar solves physical mechanics, equilibrium, dynamics and fluids problems accompanying PHYS 1151; mathematical techniques support those physical models.

courses.name: First-Year Seminar
courses.description: Introduces university resources, community participation and academic planning for first-year students.

category_review.locator: GE 1000 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: University transition, support resources and major exploration are orientation, not a fixed technical domain.

courses.name: First-Year Writing
courses.description: Develops research and writing across audiences and genres through workshop practice.

category_review.locator: ENGW 1111 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The workshop teaches rhetorical choices, research-based writing, audience awareness and revision in academic, professional and public communication.

courses.name: Advanced Writing in the Technical Professions
courses.description: Develops research and communication in technical and professional genres.
courses.prerequisites: ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1113 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1114 with a minimum grade of C

category_review.locator: ENGW 3302 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Technical reports, proposals and presentations are the genres used to teach audience analysis, critical research and revision; the subject is technical communication rather than engineering methods.

courses.name: Advanced Writing in the Sciences
courses.description: Develops scientific argument, evidence presentation and research-based writing.
courses.prerequisites: ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1113 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1114 with a minimum grade of C

category_review.locator: ENGW 3307 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course analyzes how scientific texts present claims and evidence and teaches scientific writing and revision; quantitative evidence is a communication object, not the primary mathematical subject.

courses.name: Interdisciplinary Advanced Writing in the Disciplines
courses.description: Develops research, revision and writing across disciplinary contexts.
courses.prerequisites: ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1113 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1114 with a minimum grade of C

category_review.locator: ENGW 3315 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Interdisciplinary professional, public and academic writing is taught through audience analysis, critical research, peer review and revision.

category_review.locator: GE 1110 official course-description block
category_review.rationale: The description centers on engineering problem formulation, design evaluation, CAD and a technical design project. This is applied engineering design, not an AI method.

category_review.locator: GE 1111 official course-description block
category_review.rationale: The description uses engineering analysis and design problems to teach computation, matrix tools and microcontrollers. Its primary domain practice is engineering problem solving; it is not evidence of an AI specialization.

courses.name: Seminar for CS 1800
courses.description: Reinforces CS 1800 discrete-structures material through seminar discussion, quizzes and assignments.

category_review.locator: CS 1802 seminar description, together with CS 1800 discrete-structures description and reciprocal corequisite conditions
category_review.rationale: The seminar accompanies the explicitly reviewed discrete-structures course and reinforces its mathematical topics through discussion and assignments.

notes: All local major-page tables and prose rules are represented, including course bundles, writing alternatives, GE credit allocations, placement substitutions, integration reuse, NUpath gaps and the 2.000 CHME GPA minimum. Linked university, college and NUpath policies are not fully incorporated; curriculum remains partial.

The current chemical-engineering department page and old detailed-requirements URL retain data-science URL/PlusOne residue. The requirements link redirects to the current 2026–2027 Chemical Engineering and Artificial Intelligence BSChE catalog; legacy data-science curricula were not silently substituted.

No family inheritance is asserted in this bounded discovery pass. The AI component resembles the DS-based environmental-engineering variant, but shared policies and all bindings require an independent family review. The existing 23 family variants are unchanged.
First offering and formal program launch remain unknown. Course descriptions, prerequisites and split bundle credits remain missing unless the local table states them.

Degree correctness audit: footnote 1 permits GE 1110 plus GE 1111 instead of GE 1501 plus GE 1502. The two complete pairs are an alternative; repeated Cornerstone rows allocate credits across degree areas and do not create fixed extra enrollments. Both new course identities and four-hour values are independently checked in the GE subject catalog.

Degree audit: CS 1802 is the explicitly specified one-hour corequisite seminar for fixed CS 1800. Its requirement is a child of CS 1800, supported by the degree preamble and reciprocal CS catalog corequisite conditions; other prerequisites have not been promoted to degree requirements.
